linkedin.documentTitle: How Long Roofs Last in Oregon
linkedin.text:
Most asphalt shingle roofs in western Oregon last 20 to 30 years. The interesting part isn't the range, it's what moves a specific roof within it, and summer is the one season homeowners can actually see the evidence in good light on dry shingles.

What 10+ years on Portland metro roofs taught us: an Oregon roof almost never dies of sunburn. We're gentle on shingles where hail and extreme heat are concerned, and hard on them with eight months of moisture, moss that never takes a year off, and winter windstorms testing every seal strip. That's actually good news, because moisture problems are manageable. The early-retirement list (established moss, clogged drainage, poor attic ventilation, rushed installation, pressure washing) is the same short list that, done right, pushes a roof toward the top of its range.

The guide covers the full breakdown, including how to read your own roof's age from granule loss, color patches, and curling edges. If you don't know your roof's installation date, a free assessment can estimate remaining life from condition, and that number is the foundation of every good replacement decision.

gmb: How long does a roof last in Oregon? Most asphalt shingle roofs in western Oregon last 20 to 30 years. Architectural shingles installed to spec and maintained well sit at the top of that range and beyond, while neglected builder-grade shingles retire near the bottom. Our climate spares roofs the hail and extreme heat that kill shingles elsewhere, but delivers eight months of moisture, persistent moss, and winter windstorms. Oregon roofs rarely die of sunburn; they die of moisture, and moisture is manageable. The biggest life-shorteners are moss left to establish, clogged gutters and debris, poor attic ventilation, rushed installation, and pressure washing. The extenders are regular cleaning and moss treatment, clear drainage, healthy ventilation, and small repairs handled early. Summer's good light and dry shingles make it the easiest time of year to check for granules in the gutters, patchy color loss, and curling edges.
